review_evidence: Item-by-item review for route accuracy, age fit, distinct support stages, unseen independent and assessment material, deterministic masterclass answers, and flexible constructed grading.
title: Between Home and School
source_note: Aligned to the NCERT chapter title and themes of walking to school, landmarks, routes, fields, groves, and canals. All Zidd passages, directions, and feedback are original.

levels.title: Notice landmarks on a school route
levels.focus: find route details and distinguish places passed from the destination
levels.teaching_goal: Read original home-to-school routes and identify landmarks, movement, and destination details.

guided_check.teaching_block: A landmark is a place or object that helps us know where we are. Circle the movement word, then notice what the walkers pass. School is the destination, not every place on the way.
guided_check.passage: Nina walks past a pond and a tea shop before she reaches school.
guided_check.prompt: Which landmark does Nina pass first?

bridge.teaching_block: Read the route from start to finish. Separate where a child stops from what the child only passes.
bridge.passage: Harsh passes the post office, waits at the crossing, and then enters the school gate.

masterclass.teaching_block: Track both walkers. The question asks for a shared landmark, so reject a place seen by only one child.
masterclass.passage: Mina passes a bakery and the old well. Jo passes a clinic and the old well. They meet beside the well.
masterclass.prompt: Name the place that Jay and Noor both pass.

independent_check.teaching_block: Read without choices. A crossing point is not always the final destination.
independent_check.passage: Aman leaves the narrow lane, crosses the main road with the guard, and continues to the blue school building.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use landmark reading on a route to a sports class. Name the object passed just before the destination.
transfer_check.passage: Leela walks by the fountain, turns at a clock tower, and enters the skating rink.
transfer_check.prompt: Which landmark comes just before the skating rink?

levels.title: Follow a route step by step
levels.focus: use first, next, then, and finally to order movement
levels.teaching_goal: Sequence route steps and notice when a direction has been placed out of order.

guided_check.teaching_block: Route words show order. Start at first and move one step at a time. If you jump to finally, you may miss the turn.
guided_check.passage: First, Ritu leaves home. Next, she crosses a bridge. Finally, she reaches school.
guided_check.prompt: What happens next after Ritu leaves home?

bridge.teaching_block: Use place logic when only some time words are given. A child must reach the gate before entering the classroom.
bridge.passage: Keshav walks along the lane. Then he reaches the school gate. After that, he enters his classroom.
bridge.prompt: Which step happens after he reaches the gate?

masterclass.teaching_block: A route can be told backwards. Rebuild it from the starting point before choosing.
masterclass.passage: At last, Pia reaches the library. Before that, she turns right at the park. She began at the bus stop.
accepted_answers: the bus stop, the park, the library

independent_check.teaching_block: Order the jumbled steps. Use each step once and keep the route sensible.
independent_check.passage: Steps: enter the school / cross the canal bridge / leave the farm gate
independent_check.prompt: Write the three steps in order.
accepted_answers: leave the farm gate, cross the canal bridge, enter the school
leave the farm gate; cross the canal bridge; enter the school

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer sequencing to a fire drill. Safety directions also depend on order.
transfer_check.passage: Steps: gather at the field / walk down the stairs / leave the classroom
transfer_check.prompt: Put these safety steps from start to finish.
accepted_answers: leave the classroom, walk down the stairs, gather at the field
leave the classroom; walk down the stairs; gather at the field

levels.title: Work out route words from clues
levels.focus: infer the meanings of route, grove, canal, and branch from context
levels.teaching_goal: Use nearby descriptions to understand landscape and route vocabulary.

guided_check.teaching_block: A meaning clue often follows the new word. Read beyond the word before choosing. Do not choose a meaning only because it sounds alike.
guided_check.passage: We rested in a grove, a small group of mango trees growing together.

bridge.teaching_block: Look at what the place carries or contains. The action can tell you what kind of place it is.
bridge.passage: A narrow canal carries water from the river to the fields.
bridge.prompt: What is a canal in this sentence?

masterclass.teaching_block: Use both sentences. A route is the way followed, not the speed or the traveller.
masterclass.passage: Our usual route goes past the temple. Today that way is closed, so we take another road.
options: the way from one place to another
accepted_answers: the way from one place to another

independent_check.teaching_block: Infer the body part of the tree from the action described.
independent_check.passage: The squirrel ran along a branch that grew out from the tree trunk.
accepted_answers: a part that grows from a tree trunk

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use context clues in a garden, away from the school route.
transfer_check.passage: The gardener dug a shallow channel so rainwater could flow toward the pumpkin bed.

levels.title: Tell the main route clearly
levels.focus: choose important route information and leave out side details
levels.teaching_goal: Retell the main path in a short sentence without copying every detail.

guided_check.teaching_block: A route summary keeps the start, key path, and destination. It leaves out small details such as bag colour. Compare each choice with the whole route.
guided_check.passage: Zoya leaves her flat, walks through Green Park, and reaches school. She carries a purple bottle.
guided_check.prompt: Choose the sentence that keeps Sahil's route and leaves out side details.
options: Zoya walks from her flat through Green Park to school.
accepted_answers: Zoya walks from her flat through Green Park to school.
zoya goes from her flat through green park to school

bridge.teaching_block: Join repeated steps into one clear line. Keep places in order and remove comments that do not change the route.
bridge.passage: Irfan starts at the farm. He follows the canal. He crosses the stone bridge and arrives at school.
options: Irfan goes from the farm along the canal and over the bridge to school.
Irfan likes stones near his farm.
School has a bridge inside it.
accepted_answers: Irfan goes from the farm along the canal and over the bridge to school.
irfan follows the canal and crosses the bridge on his way to school

masterclass.teaching_block: A strong summary includes the route's change. Check whether the choice explains why the child uses a different way.
masterclass.passage: The short lane is muddy today. Sumi uses the longer market road and still reaches class on time.
masterclass.prompt: Which sentence best summarizes the route change?
options: Sumi takes the market road because the short lane is muddy.
Sumi is always late on the short lane.
accepted_answers: Sumi takes the market road because the short lane is muddy.
sumi uses the longer market road because the lane is muddy

independent_check.teaching_block: Retell only the route. Include the start, two useful landmarks, and the destination in your own wording.
independent_check.passage: Bimal begins at the bus shelter. He passes the water tank, turns beside the banyan tree, and reaches the music school.
independent_check.prompt: Summarize Bimal's route in one sentence.

concept_slots.description: Includes the bus shelter as the starting point.
Includes both the water tank and banyan tree.
any_of: passes the water tank and turns by the banyan tree

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the same summary skill for a nature trail. Keep the route order and destination, not the weather detail.
transfer_check.passage: The trail begins at the visitor hut. It bends around a pond, climbs past three rocks, and ends at a bird hide. A cool wind blows.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one sentence that summarizes the trail.

concept_slots.description: Includes the pond and rocks in route order.
Includes the bird hide as the end.

levels.title: Give safe, complete directions
levels.focus: write route directions with movement words and landmarks
levels.teaching_goal: Give concise directions that another child can follow safely.

guided_check.teaching_block: Good directions begin from a known place and use a clear movement word. Include a safe crossing point when the route mentions one.
guided_check.passage: From the school gate, walk to the zebra crossing. Cross with the guard and turn left at the library.
guided_check.prompt: Which first direction is useful and safe?
options: Walk from the gate to the zebra crossing.
Run across any part of the road.
accepted_answers: Walk from the gate to the zebra crossing.

bridge.teaching_block: Choose directions that include both the turn and the landmark. Left without a place can confuse the listener.
bridge.passage: From the clinic, go straight to the fruit shop. Turn right there to find the park.
bridge.prompt: Which direction clearly gives the turn?
options: Turn right at the fruit shop.
accepted_answers: Turn right at the fruit shop.
turn right by the fruit shop

masterclass.teaching_block: Check each instruction for order, location, and safety. The correct set must not reverse the turn.
masterclass.passage: Start at the post office. Walk past the bank. Use the crossing, then turn left for the school.
masterclass.prompt: Which direction keeps the route correct?
options: Pass the bank, cross safely, and turn left for the school.
Turn right before the bank and run across.
Begin at the school and walk to the post office.
accepted_answers: Pass the bank, cross safely, and turn left for the school.
walk past the bank, use the crossing, and turn left to school

independent_check.teaching_block: Write directions from the facts. Include the starting place, landmark, turn, and destination; wording may vary.
independent_check.passage: Start: dairy booth | walk to neem tree | turn right | destination: playground.
independent_check.prompt: Give one or two clear directions.

concept_slots.description: Uses the neem tree as the landmark.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer direction writing to finding a stall at a fair. Include each useful step and do not invent a road crossing.
transfer_check.passage: Fair map: entrance -> walk past puppet stage -> turn left at water stand -> seed stall.
transfer_check.prompt: Tell a visitor how to reach the seed stall.

concept_slots.description: Says to pass the puppet stage.
Says to turn left at the water stand.
any_of: turn left at the water stand
take a left by the water stand

items.passage: Anu passes a milk shop, waits beside the signal, and then walks into school.
Jay and Noor use different lanes, but both cross the wooden footbridge before class.
items.prompt: Which landmark is on both routes?

items.passage: Pema turns away from the market and enters the lane beside the fire station.
items.prompt: Which place is beside the lane?

items.passage: The children pass a pond and a field before reaching the red gate.
Steps: reach the corner / leave home / turn toward the school
options: leave home, reach the corner, turn toward the school
reach the corner, turn toward the school, leave home
turn toward the school, leave home, reach the corner
accepted_answers: leave home, reach the corner, turn toward the school

items.passage: First Kavya closes her gate. Next she follows the lane. Finally she enters the art room.
items.prompt: What happens next after she closes the gate?

items.passage: Steps: cross with the guard / walk to the crossing / continue to the library
accepted_answers: walk to the crossing, cross with the guard, continue to the library
walk to the crossing; cross with the guard; continue to the library

items.passage: Words: past / walks / the temple / farah
A cluster is a group of houses built close together.
The path curves around the lake instead of staying straight.
The lane is narrow, so only one bicycle can pass at a time.
A footpath is a small track made for people walking, not for cars.
Sahil starts at the orchard, follows the river path, crosses a bamboo bridge, and reaches the village school.
items.prompt: Which sentence gives the main route?
options: Sahil goes from the orchard along the river and over the bridge to school.
The school is inside the river.
accepted_answers: Sahil goes from the orchard along the river and over the bridge to school.

items.passage: Rain closes the low bridge, so Uma follows the hill road to reach class.
options: Uma uses the hill road because the bridge is closed.
Uma does not go to class.
The hill road is under the bridge.
accepted_answers: Uma uses the hill road because the bridge is closed.
uma takes the hill road because rain closed the bridge

items.passage: Mohan leaves the temple square, passes a hand pump, turns at the tailor shop, and reaches the community hall.
items.prompt: Summarize Mohan's route in one sentence.

concept_slots.description: Includes the hand pump and tailor shop.

items.passage: The garden walk starts at the shed, circles the lily pond, passes the compost pit, and ends at the greenhouse.
items.prompt: Retell the main route without copying every word.

concept_slots.description: Includes the lily pond and compost pit.

items.passage: Map facts: start at the library; walk past the bus shelter; turn right at the pharmacy; stop at the clinic.
Safe route facts: use the zebra crossing; wait for the guard; walk to the sports gate.
options: Wait for the guard and use the zebra crossing.
Run across before the guard arrives.
accepted_answers: Wait for the guard and use the zebra crossing.
wait for the guard and cross at the zebra crossing

items.passage: Directions facts: start at the yellow kiosk; pass the fountain; turn left at the flag; reach the craft tent.
items.prompt: Give the directions in one or two sentences.

concept_slots.description: Gives a left turn at the flag.
any_of: take a left by the flag

items.passage: Route facts: begin at the grain shop; follow the wall; turn right at the peepal tree; arrive at the health centre.
items.prompt: Write clear directions for a visitor.

concept_slots.description: Gives a right turn at the peepal tree.
any_of: turn right at the peepal tree
take a right by the peepal tree
